title: Gaja Capital to Become First Indian PE Firm to Go Public With ₹550 Crore IPO
excerpt: Gaja Alternative Asset Management opens its IPO on August 19 with a price band of ₹152-160 per share, marking a first for India's private equity industry.
body:
• Gaja Alternative Asset Management will open its ₹550-crore IPO on August 19, becoming the first standalone private equity firm in India to go public.
  • The price band is set at ₹152-160 per share, valuing the company at approximately ₹2,256 crore at the upper end.
  • Founded in 2004 by Gopal Jain, Gaja Capital manages India-focused alternative investment funds across education, consumer, and financial services sectors.
  • The firm raised ₹125 crore in a pre-IPO round from HDFC Life, SBI Life, and other institutional investors at a ₹1,625-crore valuation.

Gaja Alternative Asset Management, which operates under the Gaja Capital brand, will launch its initial public offering on August 19 with a price band of ₹152-160 per share — a landmark listing that makes it the first standalone private equity firm in India to go public.

The IPO, sized at ₹550 crore, comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth ₹450 crore and an offer for sale amounting to ₹100 crore by existing shareholders, including promoters. Anchor investor bidding opens on August 18, with the public subscription window closing on August 21, according to the company's red herring prospectus.

A PE Pioneer Goes Public

Founded in 2004 by Gopal Jain, Gaja Capital has spent two decades as a mid-market growth-capital investor focused on Indian entrepreneurs. The firm has built a portfolio spanning companies such as TeamLease, Lighthouse Learning, RBL Bank, John Distilleries, Xpressbees, Educational Initiatives, LeadSquared, and Signzy — primarily across education, consumer services, and financial services.

The company transitioned from a private limited to a public limited company in January 2025 and was renamed Gaja Alternative Asset Management Ltd. Former SEBI Chairman U.K. Sinha was appointed non-executive chairman as part of a board restructuring ahead of the listing.

"We have chosen to go public to strengthen our platform, deepen our commitment to investors, and seed the next generation of funds."

— Gopal Jain, Managing Director and CEO, Gaja Alternative Asset Management

IPO Structure and Use of Proceeds

At the upper end of the price band, Gaja will command a post-listing market capitalization of approximately ₹2,256 crore. Each share carries a face value of ₹5, and the minimum lot size for retail investors is 93 shares.

The company plans to deploy ₹372 crore from the fresh issue toward fulfilling sponsor commitments in its Fund IV vehicles — Gaja Capital India Fund 2020 LLP and Gaja Capital India Fund 2021 — and repaying a bridge loan. Additional proceeds will fund sponsor commitments in a proposed Fund V and a Secondaries Fund, with the remainder allocated to general corporate purposes.

The IPO has been trimmed from the originally proposed ₹656 crore filing in December 2025. Of the total issue, 50% has been reserved for qualified institutional buyers, 15% for non-institutional investors, and 35% for retail investors. Listing is expected on both the BSE and NSE on August 26.

Financial Track Record

Gaja reported a net worth of ₹575 crore and ₹62 crore in profit for the first half of FY26, with profit margins expanding to 56% during the period, according to its filing with SEBI. The firm had raised ₹125 crore in a pre-IPO round that valued it at ₹1,625 crore, with investors including HDFC Life, SBI Life, Volrado, and One Up.

Promoters Gopal Jain, Ranjit Jayant Shah (Executive Vice-Chairman), and Imran Jafar (Executive Director) will dilute part of their holdings through the offer for sale. Other selling shareholders include early investor Sanjay Hiralal Patel and independent directors.

Market Context

Gaja's IPO arrives at a time when India's alternative asset management industry is maturing rapidly. The firm manages India-focused funds including Category I and Category II alternative investment funds and advises offshore funds that provide capital to Indian companies — a structure that bridges domestic and international capital flows.

JM Financial and IIFL Capital Services are the book-running lead managers, while MUFG Intime India serves as registrar. The IPO received SEBI approval through the confidential filing route in October 2025.

For investors, the offering represents a rare opportunity to gain exposure to India's private equity ecosystem through a publicly traded vehicle — a model more common in the U.S. and Europe but largely untested in Indian markets.
